   <title>〜へ (he)</title>

   &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <span style='FONT-SIZE: 16px;'><b>Meaning</b>: indicates direction of verb. Also pronounced 'e' </span><BR />
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <strong>Example</strong>: <i>I will go abroad next year.</i><BR>
   <BR />

<br />
Such as:<br />
<br />
えきにいきます。- I'm going to the train station.<br />
<br />
 へ can replace に and vice versa. <br />

items.title: 〜へ (he)
items.description_raw_html:
〜へ (he)

    Meaning: indicates direction of verb. Also pronounced 'e'
    Example: I will go abroad next year.

  [ View this entry online ]

  Notes:  
へ and に there is no difference. They can both be used and are considered interchangeable. I see both に and へ in writing and talking.

Such as:

えきにいきます。- I'm going to the train station.

へ can replace に and vice versa.


  Examples:  
Note: visit WWWJDIC to lookup any unknown words found in the example(s)...
Alternatively, view this page on POPjisyo.com or Rikai.com

  • 私は来年外国へ行きます   [ex #648]
    • I will go abroad next year.
  • ＜乗客への呼びかけ＞（バスの）中へお詰め願います。   [ex #4808]
    • Pass along the bus, please.
  • 1000人もの人がそのパーティーへやってきた。   [ex #4809]
    • No less than 1,000 people came to the party.
  • ７月のある日、私たちは海へ行った。   [ex #4810]
    • One day in July we went to the sea.

Help JGram by picking and editing examples!!
  • Search big database for more examples of 〜へ
  • Add an example sentence
  • Detailed example form
  See Also:  
  • ni
[ Add a See Also ]

  Comments:  
  • also used as a shortcut in email as in
    　　DCへ
    　　->this part is to DC:
    (contributor: dc)
  • ? it would be nice to get an explanation of difference between ni and he.
    ロンドンに行く＝ロンドンへ行く
    ロンドンでお会いしましょう？ (contributor: dc)
  • "In motion constructions -ni and -e appear to have the same distribution [...]. The primary difference in distribution is that -ni may occur in other verbal contexts, as I show below, but -e may not, while -e may appear marking arguments in nominal constructions but -ni may not, [...]" (contributor: Amatuka)
  • In theory へ is for movement in a direction, while に implies arrival at a specific destination.
    [or some such]. In practise there is very little difference. (contributor: Amatuka)
  • N = noun (contributor: Amatuka)
  • Note: Apart from the
    DCへ
    letter / email addressing type usage you can't use へ to indicate going to a person.
    e.g. (BAD) DCへ行きました。[DC he ikimashita] I went to DC.
    (GOOD) DCの家へ行きました。[DC no ie he ikimashita] I went to DC's house. (contributor: Amatuka)
  • I'd get rid of the above 'bad' example, because DC is also a place (Washington DC), in which case you CAN say "DCへ行きました。" Put some other person's name in that to make your point, and then please delete this comment :) (contributor: Anon)

    [ Add a Comment ]
